ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creates UIAF) as amended by Ley 1121 de 2006; Ley 2010 de 2019, art. 52, Decreto 830 de 2021 and DIAN Resolución 000164 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF); Circular Básica Jurídica, Circular Externa 029 de 2014 (SARLAFT system and SFC AML/CFT chapters); Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. statute); Ley 1735 de 2014 and Decreto 1357 de 2018 (fintech/collaborative financing framework); Ley 2195 de 2022 (corporate transparency and compliance programs). Note: SFC Circular Básica Jurídica requires financial-sector licensees to identify UBOs from 5% of capital as an enhanced control applicable to the high-risk P2P micro-lending scope, notwithstanding the 25% general corporate UBO threshold.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of the foreign shareholder/parent entity (Certificado de Existencia y Representación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, Companies House, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Colombian Consular Legalization required for non-Hague Convention origin countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General Special Power of Attorney granted to the local formation agent or legal representative (Poder Especial)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction or a Colombian Notaría Pública
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian notarial authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of passports of all UBOs and subscribed shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent civil registry authority in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian Consular Legalization (non-Hague origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificates (Certificado de Antecedentes Judiciales/Penales) for directors, legal representatives and compliance officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National or state police / judicial records authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian Consular Legalization (non-Hague origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and solvency confirmation letters for all funding sources of the platform
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or licensed financial institution providing the reference
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian Consular Legalization (non-Hague origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) signed by each incorporator and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Formation agent/local counsel authenticated before a Colombian Notaría Pública

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under FATF Recommendations 12 and 22: positive verification against OFAC Consolidated SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU autonomous sanctions lists, and domestic lists maintained by UIAF, Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, Procuraduría General and Contraloría General; PEP classification of shareholders, UBOs, directors and platform managers; continuous negative news and sanctions alert monitoring; geo-screening of payment rails (ACH and local wallets) against OFAC embargoed jurisdictions; enhanced risk scoring and transaction monitoring required given the ISIC 6499 high-risk special-license classification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at www.rues.org.co; name reservation and homonymy query executed through the Cámara de Comercio of the registered-office municipality (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá via its virtual portal and RUES 'consulta de homonimia' module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish using Latin-alphabet characters; acronyms must consist of Latin letters; foreign-language terms are admissible only when translated or transliterated into the Spanish alphabet and clearly readable under Spanish phonetics; numerals may appear as letters or digits; the corporate type suffix 'S.A.S.' is mandatory; reserved and confusingly similar names (homonimia) are prohibited under Article 33 Decreto 019 de 2012 and Cámara de Comercio regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected request may be remedied by filing a corrected homonymy application extending the reservation for a new 30-day window; alternatively, the applicant may file the administrative appeal 'recurso de reposición' before the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of the rejection under Article 74 of Ley 1437 de 2011, and, where the registry maintains its refusal, a residual 'apelación' may be pursued before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio; a successfully re-filed name commences a fresh 30-day reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A virtual office is tolerated only during the preliminary incorporation phase and for a dormant S.A.S. prior to regulatory licensing; it is not acceptable as the operational domicile of a licensed P2P micro-lending platform because the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia requires a physical registered office (domicilio social) in the registered municipality, dedicated compliance facilities, personnel presence, physical records retention, and local data-system access; a corporate virtual mail address may complement, but cannot replace, the physical commercial substance required for the special license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 68% – High. Licensed fintech lenders under SFC supervision are subject to scheduled and unannounced on-site inspection visits (visitas de inspección) under Decreto 2555 de 2010 and Chapter IV of the Circular Básica Jurídica; UIAF also conducts periodic AML/CFT supervisory audits under Ley 526 de 1999, and DIAN may perform unannounced verification of the registered domicile and accounting records in connection with RUBF filing and tax registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff under Decreto 3266 de 2004, as annually updated

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of private incorporation documents and power of attorney (Poder Especial and estatutos)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under Decreto 969 de 2016, fixed per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: S.A.S. incorporation filing and mercantile registration (matrícula mercantil) in RUES
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff scaled to subscribed capital and asset size

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille processing batch for foreign corporate, identity and criminal-record documents (3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's origin country and Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Subdirección de Asuntos Consulares) where domestication is required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention fixed fees per document plus administrative handling benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per translated page with notarial certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SARLAFT / AML-CFT compliance manual and PEP-screening module for the fintech lending platform

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly or fixed retainer per Decreto 1357 de 2018 and SFC instruction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated buffer of 4.5% over total pre-incorporation statutory and professional fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 2, 4, 5, 17 and 29; Código de Comercio, arts. 98-110; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Book 2, Part 2, Title 1 (RUES registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the corresponding Chamber of Commerce for the registered seat
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private deed of incorporation) registered electronically with RUES, giving rise to the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (CERL)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an S.A.S.; shares may be subscribed and paid in up to two years, and no escrow deposit is required at incorporation. The SFC P2P lending authorization, however, will impose an additional patrimonial own-funds requirement determined under Decreto 2555 de 2010, Book 2, Part 1, Title 3, as amended by Decreto 1357 de 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The board accepts the subscription of five hundred (500) ordinary shares at par value of one thousand Colombian pesos (COP 1,000) each, paid in full to the corporate treasury. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby adopted at Carrera 7 No. 71-21, Office 502, Bogotá, D.C., within the jurisdiction of the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá; the legal representative shall promptly docket the domicile with RUES. (3) Ms. [Name], identified with citizenship card No. [ID], is appointed legal representative (Representante Legal) of the Company with the amplest powers under Ley 1258 de 2008, and is authorized to execute regulatory filings with the SFC and DIAN. (4) Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed AML compliance officer. (5) Management is directed to file all incorporation, tax, industrial, and fintech licensing applications. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name pre-validation and digital signature procurement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RUES portal administered by the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá; authorized certificate authorities (Certicámara, GSE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a name availability search (Certificado de Homónimos) via the RUES online portal; reserve the company name 'SAS' suffix for up to thirty days; procure a digital signature certificate for the legal representative and all subscribing shareholders in order to enable fully electronic filing of the constitutive document.
required_dossiers: Copies of identity cards (cédula de ciudadanía) of all shareholders and officers
Foreign investor tax ID or passport if non-resident shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber denies or queries the name, file a corrected pre-validation or submit a recurso de reposición within ten business days; alternatively, request a new name reservation after resolving the conflict.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and authentication of the constitutive instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – RUES electronic registration window; notary public where real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing mandatory clauses: company name, domicile, corporate purpose, authorized/subscribed/paid capital, governance rules, term, and dispute resolution. Execute the document with digital signatures of all shareholders or in-person before a notary if real estate assets are contributed. Pay the impuesto de registro and Chamber registration fee at the same session.
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución (or notarial deed if real property contributed)
Personal data forms for each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Chamber issues a requerimiento specifying missing or defective clauses; correct and resubmit within five business days. Failing that, refile a new constitutive document; an adverse legal ruling can be challenged before the Superintendencia de Sociedades by way of a written appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile registration, impuesto de registro, and NIT issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – RUES; Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the constitutive document and the pre-RUT through the RUES single-window portal; the Chamber calculates and collects the impuesto de registro and the RUA (Renovación/Registro) fees. The Chamber electronically forwards the registration data to DIAN, which issues the NIT, and subsequently the CERL is generated as proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fees and impuesto de registro
Identification details of shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the pre-RUT or the Chamber returns a correction notice, cure the flagged items and resubmit within five business days; a Request for reconsideration can be filed within ten business days if rights are affected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate governance and statutory bookkeeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – RUES; Superintendencia de Sociedades
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the statutory books (shareholder register, minutes book, or their electronic equivalents) with RUES; file the first board resolution appointing the Representante Legal and AML compliance officer; file the beneficial ownership information; ensure the CERL is updated with the authorized signatories, and issue internal powers of attorney for the bank and SFC filings.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (CERL)
Officer and legal representative acceptance letters
Beneficial ownership declaration (Formato de Beneficiario Final)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any book registration or beneficial ownership declaration is flagged for inconsistency, amend the request and refile with RUES; in case of silent denial, lodge a recurso de reposición within ten days or apply to the Superintendencia de Sociedades for adjudication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SFC P2P lending authorization and UIAF AML registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC); Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Solicitud de Autorización de Plataforma de Financiación Colaborativa through the SFC's electronic window (SIAC), attaching corporate governance, own-funds projection, technological risk, and AML compliance documentation. Concurrently register the company as a reporting entity (sujeto reportante) with the UIAF and adopt the SAGLA (Sistema de Administración del Riesgo de Lavado de Activos y Financiación del Terrorismo) manual.
required_dossiers: SAGLA AML manual and risk matrix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon an SFC requirement for additional information, respond within the granted term, not exceeding one month, or the application is deemed withdrawn; any rejection may be appealed through a recurso de reposición before the SFC and, ultimately, through an annulment action before the Council of State. Correcting capital or governance shortfalls and refiling is also permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, environmental, fire safety, and occupational licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente de Bogotá; Agencia Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA); Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos; Secretaría Distrital de Planeación; Ministerio del Trabajo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Procure the Certificado de Uso del Suelo confirming that the registered office may host financial technology and back-office operations; obtain the Certificado de Bomberos after an on-site fire-prevention inspection; register the Reglamento de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial with the Ministry of Labor, affiliate the workforce with an ARL at the appropriate risk class, implement solid-waste and electronic-waste segregation protocols, and verify that the physical premises meet the seismic/structural requirements of NSR-10.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title of the registered office
Floor plan and architect's structural stamp
Fire extinguisher and evacuation plan certificate
Reglamento de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal or environmental authorities may issue an inspection deficiency report; implement corrective measures and apply for a re-inspection. If an environmental classification is contested, appeal the administrative act before the respective agency or request a modification of the internal waste management plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) for the P2P micro-lending authorization; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente de Bogotá and Agencia Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for environmental/physical compliance of the operating office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización para Operar como Plataforma de Financiación Colaborativa (crowdlending segment) under Decreto 2555 de 2010, Book 2, Part 1, Title 3, as amended by Decreto 1357 de 2018

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Agencia Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) – Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente de Bogotá (local enforcement window)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the platform operates as an office-based financial technology service with negligible environmental footprint; no full EIA or environmental license is required under Decreto 1076 de 2015; a non-industrial commercial activity registration may be required by the municipal environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; compliance with ANLA Resolución 631 de 2015 thresholds is not applicable to office use. Solid waste must be segregated under Resolución 2184 de 2019; electronic and hazardous waste from IT equipment (servers, UPS batteries, e-waste) must be managed under Resolución 1362 de 2007 through an authorized gestor; ambient noise must not exceed 65 dB(A) at the property boundary per Resolución 627 de 2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Bomberos) from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos after inspection of extinguishers, alarms, and evacuation routes; structural load and seismic safety certificate in accordance with NSR-10 (Ley 400 de 1997); land-use certificate (Certificado de Uso del Suelo) from Secretaría Distrital de Planeación; mandatory employee health and safety registration with Ministerio del Trabajo (Reglamento de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial) and ARL affiliation covering occupational risk; for critical hardware rooms, additional UPS, ventilation, and fire-suppression inspection may be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – portal: www.dian.gov.co (MUISCA and VUCE platforms for taxpayer services, registration, and electronic invoicing validation)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by registering with DIAN through a duly appointed legal representative or apoderado in Colombia. The process begins by filing the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) via the MUISCA electronic portal, submitting the certified corporate existence documents (e.g., certificate of incorporation and bylaws) apostilled or legalized, the power of attorney granted to the Colombian representative, and proof of foreign exchange authorization if required. After issuance of the NIT and RUT, the entity must register for the applicable tax regime (common VAT regime, income tax, withholding agents) and enroll for electronic invoicing. Branches or subsidiaries organized as local SAS entities automatically receive a NIT upon incorporation with the Chamber of Commerce.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide US-style check-the-box elections. Colombian SAS entities are taxed at the corporate entity level and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Available statutory mechanisms include: (i) the simplified taxation regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación – RST) for eligible enterprises meeting gross-revenue thresholds (option to replace income tax and complementary taxes with a simplified levy, subject to DIAN consent), (ii) the Zona Franca regime for qualifying industrial or commercial operations (reduced CIT rate of 20% subject to employment and investment requirements), and (iii) certain hybrid mismatch adjustments under Law 2277/2022 and OECD BEPS-aligned rules that limit deductions for payments subject to no or low taxation in the recipient jurisdiction. No check-the-box election is available for the Colombian SAS; full entity-level taxation applies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for corporate entities (SAS); VAT registration and collection are mandatory from the first taxable operation in Colombian territory. For resident natural persons qualifying under the simplified VAT regime, the threshold is gross income of up to 3,500 tax value units (UVT) in the prior taxable year – approximately COP 165,634,000 for tax year 2024. SAS entities are always classified in the common VAT regime regardless of revenue level.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta – FEV) is mandatory for all VAT-registered parties with business operations. Companies must use DIAN-authorized technological providers (proveedores tecnológicos) or DIAN's free issuing application, issuing each invoice through an authorized software system that transmits the invoice and constituent elements to DIAN in real-time. DIAN must validate the invoice before the purchaser may exercise tax credits; upon validation, a CUNE (Número Único de Facturación Electrónica) is issued. In addition, equivalent electronic documents (such as credit notes, debit notes, and export supporting documents) must be reported through the RADIAN system. Real-time digital stamping is not a separate process; instead, the mandatory pre-validation by DIAN applies. For business-to-consumer transactions, the platform must likewise issue the electronic invoice or an equivalent ticket through the authorized system, unless an exemption applies (e.g., certain no-tax-special regime transactions).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to the export of goods from Colombia and to the provision of qualifying export services. For services, including digital financial or platform services, the exporter must demonstrate that the service is rendered to a non-resident recipient with the economic and effective use of the service occurring entirely outside Colombia, and obtain and preserve the supporting documentation (International Service Export Form, Declaration of Export of Services, and proof of foreign payment). Goods exports require an exit customs declaration and compliance with free-zone or Aduana procedures as applicable. In all cases, the zero-rating leaves the exporter the right to claim refundability of related input VAT paid on costs, subject to DIAN approval.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX/Déclaration de Salida)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Truck Manifest (transport evidence issued by the carrier)
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de reembolso de divisas) or certification of receipt of payment in foreign currency from the exporter's local bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN conducts strict audits on zero-rating claims. If documentation is incomplete or false, DIAN will disallow the zero rate, reclassify the transaction as a taxable local supply at 19% VAT, and also recapture any VAT refunds previously granted. The company becomes liable for the unpaid VAT, default interest, and inflation-adjusted fines calculated on the tax understatement. Under Law 2277/2022, fraudulent submission of false documents or use of fictitious export transactions may trigger criminal tax fraud charges punishable by imprisonment (up to 60 months) and larger penalties. Additionally, the authorities may suspend or revoke the exporter's authorization to issue invoices and impose sanctions of up to 1,000 UVT for failure to comply with electronic invoicing or cross-border documentation rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) for prudential supervision and the Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF) for AML/CFT supervision; foreign exchange regulation is issued under Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015, and Circular Externa DCIN-83, with operational enforcement through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries (commercial banks and foreign exchange houses) and customs/DIAN oversight of trade and capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed floating exchange rate regime. The Colombian peso (COP) is fully convertible for current account transactions (imports, exports, services, debt servicing, and profit remittances), subject to mandatory filing of the Declaración de Cambio (Exchange Declaration, Form No. 10) with the Banco de la República through an authorized intermediary for transactions above the threshold of USD 10,000 or equivalent. Capital account operations, including foreign direct investment (FDI) into a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.), require prior foreign investment registration under Resolución 1 of 2018; unregistered investment loses access to the guaranteed remittance channel. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are freely allowed after compliance with transfer pricing documentation under Articles 260-2 of the Colombian Tax Code, with a general 1.5% remittance tax on payments to foreign beneficiaries subject to treaty relief and an additional 5% withholding tax on dividends under Law 2277 of 2022 when the beneficiary is a foreign entity not benefiting from a tax treaty. The P2P micro-lending platform's revenue stream (interest spreads and loan servicing fees) is a current account item and thus eligible for full convertibility, but platform lending operations that originate borrower repayments in COP require clear tracing of funds to maintain current-account treatment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not maintain a forced export-proceeds surrender regime. Exporters and service suppliers must repatriate and negotiate export revenues exclusively through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries. For goods exports, proceeds must be collected within a statutory window of 120 days from customs clearance; for software and digital services exports, collection must generally occur within the term agreed in the contract but not exceeding 180 days unless an extension is approved by the Banco de la República. The P2P micro-lending platform, however, is not an exporter; its material inbound flows consist of foreign capital injections and platform operational income. Inbound foreign investment equity contributions must be reported to the Banco de la República within 60 days following the remittance date using Form 10; loan repayments from Colombian borrowers do not constitute export proceeds and are treated as local circulating funds in COP. The platform must further classify any foreign currency conversion through an authorized intermediary and ensure that each commercial transaction is matched with its corresponding exchange declaration for audit trail purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as primary treasury node. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Mercury, Payoneer, or Airwallex cannot serve as the principal operating bank for the Colombian S.A.S. because Colombian foreign exchange law mandates that all cross-border capital injections and current account conversions be routed through an authorized Colombian FX intermediary. An offshore EMI holds no Colombian banking or exchange license, cannot file Form No. 10 exchange declarations with the Banco de la República, and cannot provide a local NIT-attributed account for statutory AML report filing. Cross-border EMIs are permissible only as ancillary payment acquisition rails for collecting receivables from international platform users or paying foreign technology suppliers, provided the core FX compliance and treasury settlement remain onshore at a licensed tier-1 bank. Further, any use of EMI-based settlement must be disclosed to DIAN and the UIAF, and the aggregate value routed through such channels should not exceed the platform's verified operating-expense threshold to avoid rebuttal of economic substance and potential branch/PE exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. Under SFC Circular Externa 029 of 2014 and UIAF's Customer Due Diligence rules, the legal representative of the S.A.S., together with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) where the ownership concentration exceeds 10%, must attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's designated premises. Remote onboarding is available only for a legal entity already in the bank's client registry or when the bank accepts biometric e-signature and video-call verification under strict written policies; for a newly formed S.A.S. with non-resident shareholders, Colombian banks require personal attendance of a Colombian-resident legal representative and the production of original documentation. Where a non-resident majority shareholder cannot physically appear, the bank may accept a power of attorney (poder) granted to a Colombian resident director, notarized in the shareholder's jurisdiction and apostilled before Colombian consular legalization, together with a supplementary compliance interview conducted by the bank's international office. Practical blocking risk: high; the entity should designate a local compliance-proven representative and expect a 4-8 week onboarding cycle, including independent verification by the bank's AML unit and central registry cross-checks against UIAF and OFAC lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The P2P lending platform is classified as a high-risk money-service business under FATF standards, and the S.A.S. combined structure with a foreign ultimate beneficial owner may trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD) at the bank's underwriting committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Final Beneficial Owner registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) fully filed with DIAN and detail of ownership chain through the foreign parent; (2) notarized and apostilled board resolution of the foreign investor approving the Colombian subsidiary's capitalization; (3) audited financial statements of the parent and beneficial owners for the last two fiscal years; (4) sworn source-of-wealth declarations for all UBOs; (5) written business plan demonstrating the lending algorithm, borrower KYC and loan origination compliance with Chapter IV of the Colombian Fintech Regulation (Law 1735/2014 and Decree 2555/2010 on electronic payment platforms); (6) an independent AML risk assessment report prepared pursuant to Sarlaft (Sistema de Administración de Riesgo de Lavado de Activos y Financiación del Terrorismo); (7) evidence of an on-site Colombian office, payroll records, and local director appointments to establish economic substance; (8) declaration of no prior adverse regulatory actions in any jurisdiction where the shareholder operates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volume of small-dollar loans and rapid borrower payouts may be mischaracterized as unlicensed deposit-taking or money laundering through loan proceeds, particularly where borrower repayments combine reputational and prudential red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) The statutory license for crowdfunding/peer-to-peer electronic credit under the Law 1735/2014 regime, or alternatively the duly authorized credit cooperative/financial technology registration issued by the SFC, where applicable; (2) the platform's AML transaction monitoring policy, internal STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) escalation protocol, and UIAF reporting templates; (3) algorithmic underwriting documentation proving that all borrowers are natural persons with identity verified through the national ID database and fraud scoring; (4) independent audit certificate confirming that platform float accounts are segregated, non-interest-bearing, and not used by borrowers as deposit substitutes; (5) loan book statistics showing average ticket size, tenors, and default distributions; (6) data privacy and cybersecurity policy compliant with Law 1581 of 2012 to demonstrate governance; (7) a compliance officer designation with UIAF-recognized AML certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection from a jurisdiction characterized by high money-laundering risk or where the investor's source of funds cannot be independently verified, causing the bank's correspondent clearing channels to refuse settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) For the capital contribution: Foreign Investment Registration certificate (Registro de Inversión Extranjera) issued or acknowledgment receipt from Banco de la República; (2) SWIFT MT103 trail of the inbound funding evidencing the sender's bank of record and the Colombian S.A.S. as named beneficiary; (3) formal legal opinion (dictamen legal) from a reputable Colombian attorney confirming the legitimacy of the capital routing structure and compliance with Law 9/1991 and Circular DCIN-83; (4) tax residence certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) of the foreign subscriber of shares issued by the destination country's tax authority; (5) the constitutional deed (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal) of the Colombian S.A.S. extracted from the Cámara de Comercio; (6) copy of the order of incorporation and commercial registry evidencing no disruption of the juridical person; (7) source-of-funds breakdown for any equity component above USD 100,000, to include financial statements, selling company records, or shareholder dividend evidence; (8) written undertaking to local substance commitments, such as minimum payroll headcount, IT infrastructure investment, and office lease term, validated by later documentary proof during the bank's annual file review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a wire transfer through SWIFT to the Colombian S.A.S.'s local USD or COP account held at an authorized Colombian bank. The sender must identify the ultimate investor and reference the foreign investment registration file number if a pre-registration certificate has been issued; otherwise, the S.A.S. must complete the Declaración de Cambio (Form No. 10) through the receiving authorized intermediary within 60 calendar days of the value date. The recommended SWIFT MT103 narrative must include: 'APORTE SOCIAL / CAPITALIZATION OF CO_SAS', the NIT of the Colombian entity, the full legal name and tax ID of the non-resident shareholder, and the purpose-of-payment code aligned with the capital account classification under Chapter 5 of Decree 1068/2015 (foreign direct investment in financial or non-financial corporations). The minimum equity remittance into the Colombian S.A.S. requires no statutory minimum registered capital, but a contribution of at least USD 10,000 equivalent for operational viability is recommended for bank appetite. Deposits below USD 10,000 do not require a Form 10 declaration but must still be traceable in internal accounting. Where the equity injection is accompanied by a foreign shareholder loan (quasi-equity), it must be registered as external debt with the Banco de la República and is subject to the external debt term and disbursement registration formalities under the same regulatory framework. The use of an offshore EMI as a conduit for the capital injection is disallowed; all flows must pass through a Colombian authorized FX intermediary at least once before being converted into local COP float. The receiving bank will require a board resolution, the updated certificate of incorporation, and a description of the lending platform's operating cycle. For dependency on platform investors from multiple jurisdictions, the S.A.S. should open separate client sub-accounts (fiduciary or escrow) at the same bank to segregate investor sums from the operating treasury account, ensuring an auditable trail and preventing the bank from categorizing the entity as a communal savings vehicle.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the P2P micro-lending platform are classified into four legs. Leg 1 (local borrower disbursements): COP disbursements via ACH through the CUD (Cámara de Urgencias y Descuentos) to beneficiaries' bank accounts, complementing local wallet payouts via Nequi and Daviplata; no FX regulatory filing is required given the domestic nature of these transactions, but each disbursement must be reconciled against the platform's lending ledger and the borrower's electronic KYC record. Leg 2 (repatriated investor profits and dividends): remittance of profits to the non-resident investor by SWIFT MT103 to the foreign beneficiary bank; the Colombian bank executes the transfer after verifying the Form 10 foreign investment registration, withholding the 5% dividend tax and the 1.5% remittance tax where not reduced by an applicable tax treaty; the Exchange Declaration identifies the remittance purpose as 'Rendimientos de Inversión extranjera directa' with reference to the original capital registration. Leg 3 (foreign supplier or technical platform fees): payment for software licenses, cloud hosting, and digital services to non-resident vendors via SWIFT MT103; the vendor must provide an invoice with the foreign tax ID and the local entity must perform a services-rendered benefit test to avoid characterization of a Colombian permanent establishment; the payment is subject to the 15% withholding tax on gross foreign service income (or applicable treaty reduction) and a 1.5% remittance tax unless the provider has furnished a Colombian tax ID and a contractual exemption. For operational treasury settlement with a foreign exchange house or a liquidity partner, the S.A.S. should use a USD-denominated correspondent account bridge offered by the tier-1 bank (for example, via J.P. Morgan SE or Citi as the bank's U.S. correspondent); the platform must aggregate all outbound trade-related wires under the appropriate Current Account Movement Form and monthly statistical filing to the Banco de la República (Form 310 consolidated declaration) where the total monthly volume exceeds COP 20,000,000 equivalent. Leg 4 (commercial letter of credit and trade settlement for any future loan portfolio sale or securitization): issuance of an irrevocable Documentary Credit or standby LC by the Colombian bank on behalf of the S.A.S. to a foreign purchaser or seller is legally permissible but economically rare for a micro-lending platform; the LC is valid for cross-border acquisition of credit portfolios or sale of charge-off books and must be executed in strict compliance with the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600). All outbound extended disbursements must be encrypted within the bank's approved correspondent clearing network and cannot run through an unlicensed EMI or virtual asset wallet for any part of the transaction chain, absent an exceptional SFC fintech sandbox authorization.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts (FX Forwards) between COP/USD, traded with an authorized Colombian bank where the S.A.S. proves an underlying current or capital exposure; the hedge cannot be speculative and must be recorded in the entity's hedge accounting schedule.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the COP/USD rate, entered only for the purpose of hedging the economic value of a registered foreign investment or expected loan portfolio repayment dividend, and not for generating stand-alone speculative profit; such NDFs must be separately disclosed in the transfer pricing documentation for attribution to the Colombian treasury function and cannot be executed through a Colombian branch without SFC authorization.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) structuring between COP floating-rate cash flows and USD fixed-rate cash flows, contracted with a local derivative intermediary or a foreign counterparty acting through its Colombian licensed branch, where the S.A.S. demonstrates that the swap notional equals the registered capital injection or the present value of external debt payments and is cleared through a recognized central clearing counterparty; the swap must be tied to a real cross-border treasury exposure and minuted by the board of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual renewal of the commercial registration of the S.A.S. and its establishments of commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá); registration records consolidated in RUES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year by the final business day of the month assigned to the last digit of the NIT: digits 0-1 terminate in January, 2-3 in February, 4-5 in March, 6-7 in April, 8-9 in May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a monthly surcharge on the renewal fee, administrative fines up to COP 2.5 million under Law 1727/2014, and automatic transition to inactive status in RUES; persistent non-renewal leads to administrative strike-off of the commercial registration and evidentiary weakening of the S.A.S. limited-liability shield before creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Acta de Asamblea General de Accionistas y Estados Financieros aprobados (annual general meeting minutes and approved statutory financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio for deposit of the minutes and financial statements; Revisor Fiscal opinion attached when a statutory auditor is mandated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first three months of each fiscal year, no later than March 31; for an S.A.S., shareholder decisions may validly be adopted by written resolution under Law 1258/2008 without a physical meeting, provided the document is filed within the same period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing triggers Superintendencia de Sociedades sanctions up to 200 monthly minimum wages, compulsory publication of the closing balance sheet in a widely circulated newspaper, and loss of the evidential value of the year-end accounts; repeated omission is an administrative strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return and complementary declarations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), via the MUISCA electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between April 9 and April 21 of the year following the taxable year; the exact day is set by DIAN resolution according to the final two digits of the NIT.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing sanction under Estatuto Tributario Art. 641 of 5% per calendar month or fraction thereof of the greater of income tax due or updated taxable income, capped at 100%, plus default interest; non-filing sanction may reach 20% of taxable income and enforcement includes asset seizure and public media disclosure.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday exists for P2P fintech S.A.S. entities. Available incentives include: (i) 100% taxable deduction for investments in certified science, technology, and innovation (STI) projects; (ii) an income tax credit of 25% (temporarily 50% for tax years 2023-2026) for qualified STI investments under Article 256-1 E.T.; (iii) 50% deduction for investments in alternative energy sources; (iv) income from domestic technology-based services may qualify for reduced treatment only if registered as an Orange Economy undertaking. Interest income from micro-lending is fully taxed at 35%.
